*   **Limitations:** Limited to local part addition/deletion; slow convergence; potential for blurriness without geometric constraints [S2].

The evidence in Source [S2] explicitly states that Edit-NeRF 'only supports adding or deleting local parts' (limited to local part addition/deletion) and that 'the editing process is slow due to its iterative optimization nature' (slow convergence). Regarding 'potential for blurriness without geometric constraints', the text mentions that while Edit-NeRF has limited shape operation capabilities, subsequent methods like CLIP-NeRF and others introduced 'geometric priors' (such as transmittance regularization and density constraints) to 'improve fidelity and visual quality' and address the lack of 'realism and visual appeal' in earlier models. This implies that the absence of such geometric constraints in the earlier model (Edit-NeRF) leads to lower visual quality (blurriness/lack of realism). Thus, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
supported
